title: Introduce build-accelerator daemon and shared snapshot cache to reduce cold CI latency
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: many CI jobs experience long cold-start times due to repetitive dependency extraction, language runtimes bootstrapping, and large Docker layer pulls. Current attempts at cache warmup (layered priming, ad-hoc cache copies) are brittle and require per-repo scripting. Objective: ship a cross-repo build-accelerator daemon (hosted on runners) that maintains a shared snapshot cache of pre-extracted artifacts and filesystem snapshots. The daemon will provide a simple RPC to request a snapshot by key, efficiently materialize it into the job workspace, and update metrics. Goals: reduce median cold job walltime by >=20% for the top 50 slowest CI job templates, reduce egress/storage cost compared to full artifact duplication, and be compatible with our CAS and existing build caching infrastructure.
acceptance_criteria: Daemon deployed to CI runners pool and enabled for at least 50% of Linux self-hosted runners
Median cold-start latency for target job templates reduced by >=20% measured across 2 weeks of canary runs
Cache hit rate >= 60% on canary repos without manual per-repo hooks
Fallback path: if daemon unavailable, CI job proceeds using existing caching behavior with no failures
Observability: Prometheus metrics (hit/miss, fetch latency), Grafana dashboard, and a Datadog alert for >3h daemon outage
Security: daemon runs unprivileged, respects runner IAM role, and artifacts access is audited (logs uploaded to central store)
Integration tests and e2e job templates demonstrating correct snapshot materialization included in repo
tasks: Design spec: snapshot format, key schema, retention/eviction policy, security model (2025-02-12)
Prototype daemon in Go with a small local disk-backed index (2025-02-18)
Integrate with existing CAS: fetch by digest and build snapshot if missing (2025-02-21)
Runner image update: include client and autostart unit, small init script (2025-02-24)
CI config changes: opt-in flag for jobs and example templates for Node/Python/Go (2025-02-25)
Observability: export metrics, dashboards, and add runbook entries (2025-02-26)
Canary rollout: enable on 5 repos, collect telemetry for 2 weeks, iterate (2025-03-01)
Documentation: ops runbook, developer guide, and migration notes for repo owners (2025-03-05)
comments: 2025-02-11 - Maya Patel: Kickoff meeting notes attached in Confluence. Decided to prefer snapshot materialization over container layer injection to support heterogeneous build tools.
2025-02-15 - Luca Romano: Prototype daemon can materialize compressed tar snapshots in ~1.8s for a 20MB snapshot. Trade-off: needs careful eviction to avoid disk pressure on runners.

2025-02-17 - Security review (initial): Security asked for explicit ACLs for snapshot keys and a read-only worker user; agreed to run daemon unprivileged and require runner role binding. Added auditing to requirements.
2025-02-20 - PR feedback (GH#12): Request to align key schema with CAS digest naming; implemented and pushed fix. Also added checksums to avoid partial materialization.

2025-02-24 - Benchmark: on three representative Node/Python repos, cold job median walltime improved by 28%, peak improvement 43% for dependency-heavy jobs. Will expand tests across more templates in canary.
2025-02-26 - Ops note: Rolling update script prepared. Plan: deploy daemon to staging runners, run canary on 5 repos, validate metrics for 7 days, then 50% rollout next week.
2025-02-27 - Design decision: use LRU eviction with size and age thresholds; snapshot garbage collection will run nightly. We will also support manual pinning for high-value caches.
2025-02-28 - Blocker: need disk quota enforcement on some older runner types (ticketed ENG-775002). Workaround: mark those runners as opt-out until quota patch is deployed.
